$comment: The capability inventory: what this platform can do for workflow, agents and
enterprise operation, graded against a fixed list of capabilities, and the
test that shows each claim. test/ash_enterprise/capability_inventory_test.exs
reads this file and fails when a claim outruns its evidence.
Statuses:
existing -- works, and a test named here would fail if it regressed.
partial  -- part of it works and is tested; `gap` says what is missing.
missing  -- not built. A missing row names no tests: if one demonstrates
something, the row is partial.
refused  -- deliberately not built; `gap` gives the reason. A refused row
may name the test that proves the refusal holds.
A test reference is {file, test}, where `test` is the exact name in a
`test "..."` line. A reference with `dep` points into that first-party git
dependency's own suite, read at the revision pinned below; it runs in that
dependency's CI, not this one.
`pins` records the dependency versions the claims were read against. A pin
with `lock` must equal mix.lock exactly, so moving that dependency means
re-reading the rows that name it (each row's `deps`). A pin with
`requirement` is checked against mix.lock as a version range: the claims
that rest on it are about what this application does with the dependency,
and were re-read at every version the range admits so far (`read_at`).
Last reviewed against the tree: 2026-10-27.

capabilities.summary: A process definition moves draft, published, retired; a published version is immutable and content-hashed, a running instance keeps the version it started on, and a tenant can pin a version or follow the platform baseline.
capabilities.gap: No manifest of what a version depends on (decisions, actions, models), and no promotion between environments.

tests.test: a platform binding pins a version rather than tracking the latest
a tenant binding wins over the baseline
save_xml rejects when status is not draft
second definition with same key gets version 2

capabilities.summary: Exclusive gateways with conditions and a declared default flow; the branch taken, and the expression that chose it, are recorded as process events.

tests.test: the gateway records which branch it took
a conditioned branch records the FEEL that chose it
default branch taken when no condition matches

capabilities.summary: Parallel fork and join, with a join that waits for every inbound branch and branches that may end on their own.
capabilities.gap: No concurrency limit on branches, and mixed (fork-and-join in one) gateways are refused.

tests.test: parallel process completes after join
a branch parked on an approval keeps the instance running

capabilities.summary: A parallel multi-instance activity runs once per element of a list known only at run time, and joins once.
capabilities.gap: Scalar elements only; no maximum concurrency, completion condition or partial-failure policy.

tests.test: one instance per element, and the activity runs that many times
what follows runs once, not once per element

capabilities.summary: Sequential multi-instance is refused when a diagram is compiled.
capabilities.gap: It needs a cursor on the token that the engine does not keep; a loop is modelled another way or not at all.

tests.test: a sequential multi-instance is refused with its reason

capabilities.summary: A call activity starts a child process by key; the parent waits and resumes when the child completes, and call depth is bounded.
capabilities.gap: The child resolves the latest published version when it starts rather than a pinned one, and cancelling the parent does not cancel the child.

tests.test: the child runs and the parent carries on after it
the parent waits while the child does

capabilities.summary: Message, signal and timer waits and receive tasks park a token in the database; a duplicate wake loses a compare-and-set, and a deadline on a human task is a boundary timer.
capabilities.gap: No timeout on a message, receive or call-activity wait: boundaries attach to human tasks only.

tests.test: an event carrying the right key wakes the token and the process finishes
a redelivered event wakes the token once
when the timer is due the token wakes and the process finishes
firing cancels the task, interrupts the branch, and routes out of the boundary

capabilities.summary: A cron job starts work at a set hour, and the work runs as a process with a human approval in it.
capabilities.gap: Schedules are fixed in code at compile time; there is no per-tenant schedule a person can change, and timer start events are refused.

tests.test: scheduled at the compose hour, composed by the process, approved on Today
the cron fans one sweep per configured tenant

capabilities.capability: Service tasks that call application actions
capabilities.summary: A service task names an action from an allowlist; publishing a diagram that names anything else is refused, and declared inputs reach the action.
capabilities.gap: No stable invocation key reaches the action, so idempotency under redelivery is each action's own business.

tests.test: the declared inputs reach the action
publishing a diagram that names an unregistered action is refused
inputs arrive evaluated and the promoted signal routes a following gateway

capabilities.summary: Nothing lets a worker outside the application claim a task, heartbeat and report back.
Each declared operation on an external service is a generic action with a code interface, sent through one proxy facade using the caller's own connection.
capabilities.gap: These actions are not offered to the process designer as tasks.

tests.test: every declared operation is a generic action with a code interface
the same action spends each actor's own connection

capabilities.summary: A failed service task is retried by the engine within a global attempt budget and then fails the instance; a failed instance can be resumed; external calls fail with typed reasons.
capabilities.gap: No per-node retry or timeout policy.

tests.test: exhausting the engine's attempts fails the instance and kills the token
a retry after the cause is fixed advances the instance
410 from Calendar surfaces as :gone (sync token invalid)

capabilities.summary: Compensation inside one step is available through Reactor; compensation that spans process nodes is not.
capabilities.gap: Cross-node compensation is refused by the process engine; undoing an effect is modelled as an ordinary, later action.

capabilities.summary: An instance can be cancelled (its open tasks' timers go with it), a failed instance retried, and a parked instance superseded by a fresh run of another version.
capabilities.gap: No paused state; cancelling is not one transaction and records no actor; a rerun always starts from the beginning.

tests.test: cancelling an instance cancels its open tasks' timers and records them
retry_instance resumes a failed instance once the cause is fixed
the successor starts from the beginning and parks on the target's signature

capabilities.summary: Model calls go through one guard that can confine them to in-zone models; every call, streamed or not, is recorded structurally without content; the assistant answers on a durable agent run, one guarded model call per step.

tests.test: on: a hosted call is refused before anything is sent, and the refusal recorded
a stream is recorded with its usage once it has been read
it reads in its loop across several steps, then answers with citations

capabilities.summary: Tools are actions exposed on domains, typed by their arguments and authorized as the person asking.
capabilities.gap: Every tool's action declares its effects (ash_agent's AshAgent.Effects, ADR 0057), and ACP reads them, but MCP clients do not see them yet: ash_ai sends no tool annotations from the declaration.

tests.test: the ash_ai tool surface is reads only — no run-starting tool
a member with no grants gets nothing from any tool
every domain with ash_ai tools checks them, and every tool's action is declared

capabilities.summary: An assistant answer is an agent run: one model call per job, a journal a resumed step reads, and tool calls that run once. A worker killed mid-answer leaves a run the sweep resumes, and the answer is recorded once (durability tier: test/ash_enterprise/assistant/durable_answer_test.exs).

tests.test: a model call that fails leaves the run to be tried again, not a lost answer
it reads in its loop across several steps, then answers with citations

capabilities.summary: A coding-agent tool request pauses the run until a person approves the stored request; assistant proposals change nothing until a person executes them, and execution re-checks authorization as that person.
capabilities.gap: An approval carries no digest or expiry, and nothing checks that what runs matches what was approved; client-session approvals are held in memory, and an 'always allow' answer is treated as once.

tests.test: tool request → pending invocation pauses the run → approval resumes it exactly bound
execution re-checks authorization rather than trusting the earlier check
a foreign session's ref is denied even with allow_once

capabilities.summary: Model instruments that must answer in a shape send a JSON schema on the wire and refuse output that does not decode, keeping the raw output.
capabilities.gap: Declared per instrument; an agent has no declared output type of its own.

tests.test: on the wire, Splash gets the schema as a json_schema response format, unrewritten
output that is not JSON is refused verbatim

capabilities.summary: Prompts are code modules; nothing versions them as data or ties a recorded answer to the prompt that produced it.
A model is resolved from configured profiles, and an in-zone profile wins over a hosted default.
capabilities.gap: No fallback: with no in-zone profile the assistant asks nothing rather than falling back to another model.

tests.test: with an in-zone profile it is the default, with the profile's transport
with no in-zone profile nothing is asked: no hosted fallback

capabilities.summary: The vector extension is installed in the database and unused.
Conversations are stored as threads of turns, sealed, owner-only and erasable; the next question carries the conversation so far.
capabilities.gap: A fixed window of recent turns, text only: each answer's run journals its steps, but the next question carries only the turns' text.

tests.test: the next question carries the conversation so far, as text only

capabilities.summary: An agent cannot start another agent: no run-starting action is exposed as a tool.
capabilities.gap: Refused until bounded child runs (a subset of tools and a carved-out budget) are designed.

tests.test: only the read actions are typed tools — never run-start (no nesting)

capabilities.summary: The application serves tools over MCP but consumes none from an external MCP server.
A decision table, not a model, decides whether work proceeds automatically or waits for a person, and a model's judgment is banded by a table that can send it to human review.
capabilities.gap: Where a model may and may not decide is a written convention, not something the platform checks.

tests.test: a low-risk request is granted without a human
a privileged request waits for a human instead
review records the banding, materialises no fact

capabilities.summary: An evaluation set of synthetic questions, with expected tool calls, facts and citations, scores the assistant's answers per case.
capabilities.gap: Results go to a local file; no stored history and no gate on a release.

tests.test: the oracle answers every case and scores perfectly
a wrong answer shows up as its misses

capabilities.summary: Model judgments are calibrated against human verdicts, and a calibration run that misses its own pre-registered bar proposes nothing.
capabilities.gap: Observed failures do not become regression cases in an evaluation set.

tests.test: a run that misses its own pre-registered pass bar proposes nothing
a labelling verdict appends one pair to the family's slot

capabilities.summary: Human tasks are claimed, completed, delegated, approved or rejected by their candidates; candidacy grants read access; maker-checker excludes the requester (an organization that opts in may let its only administrator approve their own agent publish, recorded as a sole-administrator approval, while no one else holds or has held the Administrator role); exactly one of several concurrent claims wins; escalation timers fire.

tests.test: a candidate with no task grant reads their task and no other
the only administrator approves their own publish, recorded as such
a second administrator added before the decision is applied makes it stale
by revoking their role is not the only administrator
compose → approval → approve completes the instance with the draft stored
a requester excluded by maker-checker cannot claim through a candidate team
a candidate delegate takes the task, and the hand-off is recorded
of several people claiming one task at once, exactly one wins
escalation timer fires

capabilities.summary: The pieces exist separately (a per-run process view, decision evaluations, model-call records, a lineage graph), but nothing joins one execution's records into one view.

capabilities.capability: An assistant that explains what happened
capabilities.summary: Assistant answers cite only the records its tools returned, and an agent can read the lineage graph as the person asking.
capabilities.gap: No tools over process instances, decisions or model calls, so it cannot yet answer why a given execution went the way it did.

tests.test: it reads in its loop across several steps, then answers with citations
the ACP prompt reads the same graph as the actor

capabilities.summary: A process designer and a decision-table editor in the browser, each offering the platform's actions or decisions as a catalogue; a tenant forks the platform baseline into its own draft, and the designer saves, publishes and discards it.

tests.test: Customize forks the baseline into the tenant's own draft
the service task panel renders the action catalogue
publish form saves then publishes

capabilities.summary: Resources, lifecycles, rules and judgment questions are declared in code through DSLs and are introspectable.
capabilities.gap: Processes have no code DSL, by choice: a diagram is the only way to write one.

tests.test: the state machine is declared on the resource, so it can be diagrammed
waiving the non-waivable floor is refused at compile

capabilities.summary: Development-time tooling for coding agents: resource introspection, synced usage rules, a runtime bridge, and a laws judge whose report reaches change review.
capabilities.gap: Here only the laws judge is exercised by a test; the introspection commands are tested in their own package, and the usage-rules sync is checked by a script.

tests.test: carries the laws judge's report unchanged and each touched candidate's fact

capabilities.summary: Authorization is a union of grants that never subtract; system actors are a closed list, and the AI actor matches no bypass.
capabilities.gap: No automation principal: work started by a schedule or a process runs as a system actor rather than a named, granted identity.

tests.test: two narrow grants union rather than conflict
the ai actor never matches

capabilities.summary: External connections are held by an integration proxy and derived from the actor; no action accepts a connection or provider credential as input.
capabilities.gap: Platform secrets are deployment configuration; nothing stops a secret pasted into ordinary input.

tests.test: no generated action has a connection or provider-config argument
a caller-supplied connection id is rejected as an unknown input

capabilities.summary: Published definitions are immutable and a tenant binding pins one; reverting a tenant's customization is deleting its binding.
capabilities.gap: No release manifest tying definitions, decisions, prompts and models together, so there is nothing to roll back as a unit.

tests.test: reverting a customization is deleting a row
reports how far behind a fork is, without diffing or merging

capabilities.summary: Event-triggered starts can be disabled without a deployment, and a single event that would start too many processes is refused.
capabilities.gap: No budgets or rate limits for agents, and the job queue's rescue and pruning are configuration with no test.

tests.test: disabling is an operational switch, not a deployment act
fan-out past max_starts_per_event is refused loudly and starts nothing

capabilities.summary: A hash-chained, per-tenant audit log the database refuses to update or delete, which detects rows altered or removed behind it; personal content is erased by destroying its key.

tests.test: an altered row is found
chains are per tenant, so one tenant's writes do not enter another's
encrypt -> read -> shred -> unreadable, structure intact

capabilities.summary: A tenant is provisioned without any outside service, and model calls can be confined to models running inside the deployment's zone.
capabilities.gap: The release migration path and a packaged deployment are not exercised by any test.

tests.test: seed_tenant/1 provisions a confirmed administrator who can sign in, and sends nothing
on: an in-zone call passes, pinned to the profile's host and key
